title: Orchestrate credential reshuffle and slim stream consumer surface (py/ts/go)
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Context: Developers have asked for a less opinionated credential lifecycle inside the SDKs so embedding token rotation and stream surface concerns in one place is easier to reason about and test. This PR extracts a lightweight Credential Orchestrator, introduces small per-language adapters, and trims blocking points in streaming consumers to improve ergonomics and parity across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Changes are intentionally conservative: the public top-level client surface remains stable where possible and a compatibility shim is provided for legacy TokenProvider shapes. Motivation: reduce duplication of token refresh logic across SDKs, make stream iteration non-blocking during reauth windows, and give ops teams telemetry hooks to attribute auth-induced latencies. Summary of changes: 1) Introduced credentials/orchestrator module (core): centralizes refresh policy, backoff profiles, jittering, and metrics tagging. 2) Added per-sdk adapters: python/adapters/credential_adapter.py, typescript/src/credentialOrchestrator.ts, go/cred/orchestrator.go. Adapters implement a small well-documented interface and are wired to each SDK's session manager. 3) Streaming ergonomics: made generator/async iterator resume non-blocking during credential renewal by allowing an in-flight request to complete while a background refresh is performed; added explicit ResumeAfterRefresh hint for clients that need deterministic ordering. 4) Backoff/retry alignment: consolidated retry presets used for auth failures across SDKs and added telemetry counters for reauth attempts and durations. 5) Shims and migration helpers: legacy TokenProvider adapter for backward compatibility and migration notes. 6) Tests and CI: added cross-sdk unit tests (mocked token server) and e2e smoke tests for streaming reconnect scenarios. 7) Version bumps: Python SDK -> 1.12.0, TypeScript SDK -> 1.28.0, Go SDK -> 1.8.3. Files changed (high level): - python/sdk/session.py (refactor: delegate token lifecycle to orchestrator) - python/sdk/adapters/credential_adapter.py (new) - python/tests/test_stream_reauth.py (new) - typescript/src/client.ts (hook in orchestrator) - typescript/src/credentialOrchestrator.ts (new) - typescript/test/stream.spec.ts (new) - go/sdk/session.go (wiring) - go/cred/orchestrator.go (new) - docs/migrations/credential-orchestrator.md (new) - examples/streaming/reauth-demo/* (updated example flow) - scripts/ci/mock-token-server/* (test helper) Design notes and rationale: The orchestrator exposes a minimal surface: getActiveToken(), leaseToken(durationHintMs), onReauth hook registration. SDK clients call leaseToken before starting long-running streams or can subscribe to onReauth to get fine-grained signals. We intentionally did not introduce a global blocking refresh on every request to avoid adding per-request latency. The ResumeAfterRefresh hint is optional: runtimes that require strict ordering can opt-in. Telemetry: every reauth attempt emits credential.renew.* metrics (count, duration_ms, result). This surfaces when auth is a dominant contributor to tail latency. Backwards compatibility: legacy TokenProvider objects are accepted by the adapter; a console deprecation notice will be emitted (30 days) when the adapter is used. Migration: docs/migrations/credential-orchestrator.md contains a short recipe: 1) Replace TokenProvider with CredentialOrchestrator adapter 2) Call leaseToken before starting persistent streams 3) Optionally wire onReauth for in-application state reconciliation. Checklist: - [x] Core orchestrator impl and adapters for py/ts/go - [x] Unit tests for adapter logic - [x] Streaming non-blocking reauth smoke tests - [x] Telemetry hooks and metrics naming - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] Version bumps and changelogs Compatibility notes: No forced API rename for top-level client methods. Some internal session manager method names were changed (session.acquire_token -> session.lease_token) and shims are present for two release cycles. Rollout plan: staged rollout (feature flag) to internal dogfood org for two weeks, then enable by default for GA. Related: ENG-7123 (auth stability), ENG-7190 (streaming ergonomics). Impact on running services: low risk; added tests and canarying recommended. CI: all checks passed except one flaky TS test that required an additional retry; retried and green. Merge: squash-merged to main. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the shims (python/sdk/compat_legacy_token.py) and the handshake semantics in TS/Go adapters. If you are an integrator maintainers for a downstream embedder, follow the migration guide in docs/migrations/credential-orchestrator.md.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: can we avoid leaking the orchestrator type into the public client surface? Suggest exposing an opaque factory and keep concrete type internal.
Aisha Kapoor: agreed, adapted—exposed only a CredentialProvider interface and kept the concrete orchestrator in internal modules. Updated docs to show factory usage.
Hannah Lee: TS test fails on Node 14 with async iterator ordering—suggest a small delay in the mock server; also add an explicit test for ordering when ResumeAfterRefresh is used.
Aisha Kapoor: added ordering test and adjusted mock server to be deterministic under Node 14; CI re-run green.
Raj Patel: telemetry metric names look good. Please document the tag sets for attribution (sdk.language, transport, op=reauth).
Aisha Kapoor: added telemetry tagging to implementation and docs.
Performance team (automated): microbenchmark shows 2-3% lower median latency on streaming happy path due to reduced per-request checks.
